intervention_scopes: Finite outcome translation/sign/scale preserves the target transform and squares variance.
Changing complete-randomization arm counts preserves the finite target but changes variance.
Fisher power regenerates alternative data at five effects under a fixed rejection rule and two sizes.
All affine-statistic breakpoints and intervening cells certify the continuous inversion; common outcome translation leaves ranks unchanged.
Nonuniform assignment weights and ties expose the failure of a strict-greater randomization tail.
Unequal within-stratum treatment fractions reveal pooled composition bias while retaining target-weighted unbiasedness.
Gaussian boundary optimization is independently searched; sign, outcome-unit and arm-label changes preserve appropriate power/allocation identities.
Removing common shocks, removing idiosyncratic shocks and enlarging existing clusters expose the information boundary.
A direct encouragement outcome increment preserves uptake but breaks the treatment interpretation of the Wald ratio.
Changing independent encouragement frequency changes the treated mixture and variance, while preserving LATE and ATE.
Nonuniform Bernoulli exposure probabilities and outcome scaling are checked against the full joint-covariance identity.
Fixed-one assignment fails target positivity; a remote spillover separately fails exposure-map sufficiency.
Opposite missing-outcome laws and their mixture preserve all observed data; actual follow-up and complete response narrow the identification set.
summary.limits: Exact bounded finite-law and known-Gaussian calculations; analytic proofs are separately author-reviewed. No finite-population CLT, generic dependent inference, empirical identification, browser QA, human certification or acceptance is implied.
rejection_scopes: fixed-one design removes center untreated-unexposed support
remote treatment violates old exposure mapping
zero population first stage for a ratio
finite encouragement sample has empty arm
finite sample ratio has zero first stage
invented respondent mean in zero-response arm
